I1.quote: H2 adsorption isotherms (99.999 %) at 77 and 87 K were obtained on a Hiden Analytical Intelligent Gravimetric Analyser (IGA-003) equipped with an ultra-high vacuum system.
I1.location: main, p. 5 (journal p. 1338), Experimental Section, Materials and Methods

I2.quote: Searched main text and SI for any carbon sorbent (activated carbon, nanotube, graphene, carbonized material) whose H2 uptake the paper measures; none found. The only sorbent measured is the cobalt MOF URJC-3; carbons appear only as cited comparisons ([43]).

I3.quote: The excess hydrogen storage capacity of the novel MOF in gravimetric terms was 3.5 wt.% at 77 K and 20 bar, and 0.23 wt.% at 298 K and 170 bar

I4.quote: The resulting Brunauer, Emmett and Teller (BET) specific surface area was 171 m2 g−1, and a pore volume of 0.076 cm3 g−1.
I4.location: main, p. 2 (journal p. 1335), Section 2 Results and Discussion; also Table 1

I5.quote: A novel URJC-3 material based on cobalt and 5,5’-(diazene-1,2-diyl)diisophthalate ligand, containing Lewis acid and basic sites, has been synthesized under solvothermal conditions.

notes: Sole measured sorbent is URJC-3, a cobalt azobenzene-tetracarboxylate metal-organic framework; protocol §3 states MOFs are not carbon sorbents, so I2 fails and the first applicable code is not_carbon. Statements that the capacity exceeds 'active carbon and purified single-walled carbon nanotubes' cite ref. [43] and are not measurements. Not a review/thesis/patent; no retraction notice; is_retracted false; no statement that the data were published before. Minor internal inconsistency in the 77 K pressure for 3.50 wt% excess (16 bar in text, 18 bar in Table 2 caption, 20 bar in Conclusions); 298 K / 170 bar (Table 3, 0.23 wt% excess) is consistent, so I3 is met regardless.
